output.reasoning_summary:
All three challenges have been refuted by the evidence:

H1 (Stock-based compensation as primary driver): E10 shows R&D stock-based compensation increased by $500 million ($1,332M in 2025 vs $832M in 2024), while E2 explicitly states the total R&D increase was $1.87 billion and was "primarily due to increases in costs related to AI and other programs" with stock-based compensation being an additional factor. Stock-based compensation accounts for only ~27% of the R&D increase, not the primary driver.

H2 (Restructuring charges as larger contributor): E14 shows restructuring charges in 2025 were $390 million (related to AI chip design convergence), and E5 shows total restructuring was $494 million in 2025 vs $684 million in 2024 - actually a decrease. This is much smaller than the $1.87 billion R&D increase driven by AI.

H3 (Non-AI programs as equal/larger contributor): E2 explicitly states the R&D increase was "primarily due to increases in costs related to AI and other programs," with AI mentioned first and the word "primarily" indicating AI was the dominant factor.

The original verdict remains SUPPORTED. Operating expenses consist primarily of R&D ($1.87B increase, primarily AI-driven) and SG&A ($684M increase, not AI-driven). The R&D increase is nearly 3x larger than SG&A, and the filing explicitly attributes the R&D increase primarily to AI-related costs.
